strings.name: Charlie Chaplin
strings.role: Actor and director · A major creator of silent comedy
strings.summary: Chaplin moved from British music halls to Hollywood, combining physical comedy, emotion and social observation through his Tramp character. Often working as actor, director, writer, producer and composer, he made films including City Lights, Modern Times and The Great Dictator. He helped creators gain control over film distribution. Scrutinized by US authorities for his political views after the war, he left the United States in 1952 and settled in Switzerland.

strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: The Tramp and feature-length comedy
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Used movement, timing and emotional characterization to give silent comedy an expressive power that crossed language barriers.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Creative independence and cinematic satire
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Co-founded United Artists and addressed social realities in Modern Times and The Great Dictator.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Dies in Switzerland
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Died at his home in Corsier, leaving films that spanned the silent and sound eras.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Receives an honorary Academy Award
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Returned to the United States about twenty years after leaving to accept an honorary award from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Settles in Switzerland
strings.timeline.event-03.text: His US re-entry permit was revoked while he was travelling to London in 1952; he subsequently settled with his family by Lake Geneva.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Releases The Great Dictator
strings.timeline.event-04.text: His first fully talking feature used dual roles and political satire to oppose totalitarianism.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Releases Modern Times
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Built a comedy around the Tramp’s experiences in industrial society, incorporating experiments with sound.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Releases City Lights
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Kept silent performance at the heart of the film despite the rise of talkies and composed its score himself.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Releases The Kid
strings.timeline.event-07.text: Combined comedy and emotional storytelling in a feature about the Tramp raising a child.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Co-founds United Artists
strings.timeline.event-08.text: Joined Mary Pickford, Douglas Fairbanks and D. W. Griffith in seeking control over distribution.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: The Tramp reaches the screen
strings.timeline.event-09.text: After joining Keystone, developed his signature character with a bowler hat, cane and oversized clothes.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Tours the United States
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Travelled with Fred Karno’s company, bringing his experience of stage comedy to America.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in London
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Both parents were stage performers. He grew up in poverty and later entered the theatre through children’s troupes.
